headline: Chips Lead a Rebound as AI Debt Worries Ease
body_html:
Semiconductors powered Tuesday's advance as anxiety over AI-related borrowing eased ahead of updates from Oracle, Alphabet and Amazon. The chip group climbed 4.39%, far ahead of every other sector we track. Of 541 stocks, 323 rose and 215 fell. MaxLinear gained 12.34%, Alpha and Omega Semiconductor 11.52% and Credo Technology 10.77%.

The rotation was clear. Materials rose 2.14%, industrials 1.13%, homebuilders 0.74% and energy 0.32%, while healthcare was essentially flat at 0.05%. Consumer shares slipped 0.26% and software lost 0.6%. Hawkins was the standout, up 13.59% to lead all gainers. The water group split sharply, with Pentair up 12.82% and Xylem down 14.28%, the session's steepest drop. Valero fell 9.23% even as the energy sector edged higher.

The pattern points to investors paying for the AI build-out, meaning the hardware and industrial gear behind it, rather than the software that runs on top. Participation was healthy, but leadership was narrow. Wednesday will show whether the rebound holds once the corporate updates arrive.

briefs.headline: AI Funding Fears Cool Before Big Tech Updates
briefs.body: Concern over how the AI buildout is being financed eased on Tuesday, giving risk appetite a lift. Investors are now looking to updates from Oracle, Alphabet and Amazon for fresh evidence on spending plans and returns. Chip stocks were the main beneficiaries of the calmer mood.

briefs.headline: AI Spending Lifts Business Equipment Purchases
briefs.body: US companies spent more on equipment in September, with the AI investment boom credited for much of the increase. The report supports the idea that corporate demand for computing hardware is feeding through to the wider economy. It fits Tuesday's strength in chips and industrial names.

briefs.headline: Investors Split on Anthropic's Possible Listing
briefs.body: Market watchers are divided over a potential public offering from AI developer Anthropic. Some see a landmark moment for the sector, while others call the prospect more fantasy than plan. The debate shows how much sentiment around AI has swung in recent sessions.

briefs.headline: Water Stocks Go Opposite Ways
briefs.body: Two of the best-known water-infrastructure names diverged sharply. Pentair rose 12.82%, among the day's biggest gains, while Xylem fell 14.28%, the largest drop in our universe. The gap shows how differently investors treated companies within the same corner of industrials.

briefs.headline: Mixed Signals on Holiday Hiring; Airline Card Fees Rise
briefs.body: Experts say seasonal hiring ahead of the holiday shopping period is sending conflicting messages about retail demand. Separately, American Airlines is raising annual fees on its rewards cards for the first time since 2018. Consumer shares slipped 0.26% on the session.

briefs.headline: Gulf Tensions and Gas Supply Cut Cloud Energy Picture
briefs.body: Yemen's Houthis said they struck Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery with a missile, and Pakistani gas buyers face a QatarEnergy supply halt lasting until year-end. Energy shares still edged up 0.32%, though refiner Valero fell 9.23% in a mixed session for the group.
